root_causes.condition: The Chaos Mesh schedule continuously spawned 55-second NetworkChaos runs every minute, partitioning the checkout pod from both Kafka pods; the resulting five-second recovery windows were insufficient to restore Kafka service.
root_causes.name: otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition

diagnosis.summary: The Chaos Mesh Schedule repeatedly applied a checkout-to-Kafka network partition. Checkout therefore could not publish order messages to Kafka and opened its circuit breaker; frontend checkout calls then exceeded the proxy timeout and produced the observed 504/error-rate alerts. Frontend, checkout, and Kafka errors are downstream effects, not independent root causes.

agent_messages: I’ll inspect the offline recording only, trace causal relationships from workload symptoms back to their smallest independent configuration or resource faults, then write the required JSON.

The incident path is clear: checkout requests time out because checkout cannot produce to Kafka. I’m now validating the Kubernetes control-plane entity that caused Kafka’s failure, rather than reporting the proxy or checkout symptoms as root causes.
